feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced. Iterations 5 and 7 held the same geometry and left S-bend and slalom at 1.0 line-loss event each, with max_error near 0.060 to 0.066 m. Iteration 8 (kp 2.2, kd 0.3, ki 0, base_speed 1.1) cut those losses to about 0.05 each, and the oval stayed at 0. So the controller side, not the geometry, is the lever that moved. Iterations 3 to 4 showed mass 0.7 to 0.6 kg changes max_error by under 0.002 m, and body_width cannot move the 0.06 m off-track limit, so neither is worth changing. This candidate holds the iteration 8 geometry and tests more damping, kd 0.35, to see whether the residual 0.05 events clear.

Decide the next geometry from the next race as follows. If line_loss_events is 0 on the oval, S-bend and slalom but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, the bend-turn authority is the limit, so try wheel_track 0.12 m, which gives more yaw per PWM difference. If line_loss_events stays at 0.05 or more on the S-bend or slalom, keep the geometry fixed and report the course position where the loss begins, since the cause is then not geometric. If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m; no run has finished yet, so this is a later step.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is 0 on all three tracks but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, set wheel_track to 0.12 m. Iterations 3 to 8 show max_error stuck at 0.061 to 0.062 m while body_width cannot move the limit, so extra turn authority is the remaining geometry lever.

If line_loss_events stays at 0.05 or more on the S-bend or slalom, keep the geometry fixed and test sensor y = 0.06 m with the same 16 mm footprints. Iterations 0 and 1 used y = 0.06 m and 0.04 m, but iteration 8's tape-detection margin at y = 0.04 m has not been tested for lag, so this checks whether forward sensing reduces overshoot at bend onset.
Only if runs complete and completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, set wheel_radius to 0.035 m. No run has finished in any iteration, so top speed is not yet the limit.
